parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Name the bacterium that causes cholera.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe how cholera is transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest and explain why cholera outbreaks are common after natural disasters.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The bacteria that cause cholera can become resistant to antibiotics by a substitution mutation.

A substitution mutation occurs when one nucleotide in the DNA sequence is replaced by a different nucleotide.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain how a substitution mutation could result in a change in the amino acid sequence of a polypeptide.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The antibiotic nalidixic acid acts as an inhibitor of an enzyme involved in DNA replication in the bacteria that cause cholera.

The gene $gyrA$ codes for this enzyme. A substitution mutation in this gene results in resistance to the antibiotic nalidixic acid.

Suggest how a change in the amino acid sequence of the enzyme results in antibiotic resistance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some of the strains of bacteria that cause cholera are resistant to more than one antibiotic (multiple resistance).

Discuss the consequences of multiple resistance for health authorities.
